title: Enterprise reserved intake: questionnaire and prioritization matrix for GPU classes, burst & scaling policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers requesting Dedicated/Reserved capacity often submit requests with inconsistent detail about SLA latency targets, throughput profiles, GPU class constraints (e.g., A100/H100 vs T4/RTX), and burst/auto-scale preferences. This creates long intake cycles and misaligned engineering commitments. Goal: Define a standardized intake questionnaire, a quantifiable prioritization matrix, and a lightweight decision flow that maps request attributes to recommended SLA targets, reserved throughput patterns, allowable GPU classes, and scaling policies. Outcome: faster intake, clearer SOWs, repeatable scoping, and predictable handoff to Sales/Infra/ENG.
proposed_solution: 1) Create a 12-field enterprise intake form for Sales/CS to capture workload characteristics (qps, concurrent requests, average/peak token lengths, streaming vs batch, P95 latency SLO, production window, data residency, encryption/KMS requirement, canary/rollout plan, regulated data flag, preemption tolerance, preferred GPU classes). 2) Build a 5-factor prioritization rubric (customer strategic value, security/compliance need, density suitability, urgency, estimated infra cost) with numeric scores that auto-classify requests into Triage buckets (Express, Standard, Deep-Eng). 3) Define a GPU-class mapping table (example: latency-critical gen models => H100/A100; cost-sensitive embeddings at scale => T4/RTX with quantization) and explicit scaling policy templates (reserved baseline + burstable pool with limits, preemption rules, cold-start mitigation). 4) Document handoff checklist and SLAs to propose in initial customer conversations.
decision_matrix: Scoring weights: strategic value (30%), security/compliance (25%), density fit (15%), urgency/time-to-prod (20%), infra cost impact (10%). Buckets: Express (score >= 80) => 2-week intake, default SLA offer: 99.9% uptime, baseline reserved throughput with 1.5x burst for short windows; Standard (60-79) => 4-week intake with scoped pilot; Deep-Eng (<60) => discovery required. GPU selection rules: If P95 < 200ms for 4k tokens => require H100/A100; if model supports 4-bit quant and cost sensitivity high => recommend T4/RTX with quantization and mem-optimized nodes. Scaling policy templates: always include a minimal warm pool, autoscale triggers based on token/sec and KV-cache hit ratio, burst cap defined as % of baseline or absolute tokens/sec, fallback model variant mapping for when capacity constrained.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form created and published in Confluence and linked from Sales playbook
Prioritization rubric implemented as a Google Sheet with auto-score and sample classification for 12 historical requests
GPU-class mapping and two scaling policy templates (low-latency, cost-optimized) reviewed and approved by Infra and Runtime leads
Handoff checklist adopted by Solutions Engineering (SE) and updated in internal intake workflow
Pilot: field 5 incoming enterprise requests through the new flow and measure intake-to-SOW time reduced by >= 30%
